To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the convergence delay bounds of path vector routing protocols are determined by two main factors: (1 ) the distance between the location of the failed link and the destination, (2 ) the length of the alternate path to reach that destination after the failure, and (3 ) the message processing delay.

BGP failover delay bounds are mainly affected by the distance from the failure location to the destination and the length of the alternate path to the destination after the link failure, while the message processing delay is the main factor that determines the convergence time in networks with rich connectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three aspects of path vector routing protocols: (1) convergence analysis of standard BGP; (2) convergence analysis of convergence enhancements; (3) convergence analysis of path vector protocols under various network topologies.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the case of single link failures, the convergence delay of path vector routing protocols is mainly determined by two important factors, namely, the distance from the destination to the failure location and message processing delay.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the convergence delay of a path vector protocol is mainly determined by the distance between the failed link and the destination and the length of the shortest path to the destination, which are both independent of the protocol's convergence enhancements.
the convergence delay bounds of a path vector routing protocol under shortest path routing are mainly determined by the network topology and the message processing delay.
the convergence delay of path vector protocols can be significantly improved only if the alternate paths are much shorter than the longest alternate paths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to reduce convergence delay, it is necessary to improve the connectivity of the network.
, for path vector protocols to provide a fast fail-over in the presence of link failure, the network must be well connected.
the convergence delay bounds of path vector routing protocols are determined by the network connectivity, failure locations, and message processing delays.
